Local files for local documents — blitz-net's file: branch serves a file: document alone; a remote page reads no local file (the founder, 2026-11-12, «Как в коде + работа»)

title: CARRY:
body: CARRY: architecture decision/changed-set-write-sites (dec-ut2clwr7): its never-list (creation, hover, active, scroll, resize, load, animation, layout) holds only with no select list open — a scroll that closes a list marks its select, as decision/select-list-changed-set (dec-vvnxavu4) states; the row takes that qualifier within its 300-character bound (the operator's relay, .andromeda/runs/2026-11-13T07-43-19-wrap/inputs/I1-route-adaptation-after-landing-2026-11-13.md.txt)

- Disabled-ness is keyed one way since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness (in every document, ratified by the founder): the `DISABLED` state (`:disabled`) reads the attribute's presence, and the pointer-move gate, `ClickTarget::Disabled`, `handle_click`'s walk gate, the Enter and Space activation and focusability read `ElementData::is_disabled` — that presence on a `button`, `input`, `select` or `textarea` alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — so `disabled="false"` and a bare `disabled` on a form control match `:disabled` and are not focusable, a bare `disabled` set after creation takes its focusability away, and a `<div disabled tabindex=0>` takes focus. dioxus-native-dom removes a falsy value of its 28 boolean attributes — upstream's `is_bool_attr` predicate since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship (`disabled`, `checked`, `hidden`, `inert` among them; a framework-written `inert: false` is removed, while a truthy `inert` (by presence on itself or an ancestor element) takes focusability, hits and the tree away from its subtree (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) and Tab reaches the buttons under `inert: false`; HTML's focus fixup is built, in every document, so a node holding focus when it comes under `inert`, a subtree moved under an inert box included, gives focus up as the mutator flushes, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing; the fixup reads `is_inert()` alone, so a focused control that no longer shows, by `hidden`, `style="display:none"` or CSS alone, keeps focus and takes keys, with no panic, the limit owned by a `CARRY:` on the entry «A11y re-read»), so a `hidden: false` element stays displayed, in the tree and in the snapshot; an attribute outside the list holding `false` is still written as `"false"`. The snapshot reads `enabled` by presence — the driver's `disabled` refusal cause is stated on the same presence reading ("the element carries the `disabled` attribute, which the snapshot reads as not enabled") and is detected on it and on nothing else: the driver refuses a `click` or a `type` as `disabled` when the snapshot reads the element not enabled, with nothing dispatched and focus as it was, and acts on the same control once it reads enabled (`stand_act_disabled.rs`), and the driver's schema defines no role or name set of its own — `checked` a native checkbox's or radio's state, else, on a checkable role, the node's `toggled` reading (`True` true, `False` and `Mixed` false; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), and `value` from the element (a `select`'s `value` `BaseDocument::select_value` — the chosen option's value, for a `multiple` select its first chosen option's in tree order, nothing with none chosen — its options, its children and those under an `optgroup`, kept in the tree as `ListBoxOption` nodes, each `selected` from its chosen state, a closed select's options under it with its select's client rect as their `bounds`, which the driver's visual lint leaves out of its overlap reading in every document with an open list's rows and groups, an open list's row reading its painted row's `bounds` (`Entry.in_select_box`, read through `closed_select_of` for a closed select's option and through `select_list_bounds` for an open list's row or group, never the role) — the stand's flight booker at boot no `overlap`, `stand_lint` reading `[0, 0, 0, 0]` — while a `multiple` select's rows and groups read their own client rects and its rows are linted as usual; a range input's `value` its current value since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction — `ElementData::range_input_value`, the formatted value a key or a pointerdown moved, while its `value` attribute keeps the boot value; a password input's value reads the fixed mask `MASKED_VALUE` where it holds text and `""` where it holds none, a file input's where its `value` attribute is non-empty — and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a password's typed text is in no painted frame either: blitz-paint paints its value as bullets, its caret at the bullet of its caret index, in every document and through every renderer that paints with blitz-paint, windowed included (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12), two values of one length painting byte-identical frames, focused or not, in both layout modes (`password_painted_masked.rs`); a click inside a field holding a value places the caret by the bullets — `click_password_input` lays out one U+2022 per character through `BaseDocument::layout_as_text_input`, finds the bullet under the point and moves the real editor to that character, so no width of the real characters reaches the caret: two values of one length read one index, in both layout modes (`password_caret_click.rs`; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); the windowed paint is not run; a textarea's typed text reads back as its `value`, proven on an in-file fixture where it is named by `aria-label`), and `focused` from the tree, and `clickable` (a `bool` after `focused`, true where the vdom walk's current listeners hold `click` and the element is no disabled form control; `Snapshot::to_text` writes the token `clickable` after `focused` only when true, and `Snapshot::diff` reads it as `Reading::Clickable`) — focus proven after a click, a Tab press and Shift+Tab (`stand_snapshot_state.rs`). The snapshot's text form (`Snapshot::to_text`) reads that model, never the tree or a control: one line per node, its role and name the node's, with no second mapping (`stand_snapshot_text.rs`). The text's parts (`Snapshot::text_parts`, `TextPart`) are one more reader of that model through the text form and of nothing else — consecutive pre-order lines of `to_text`, never a split line, the parts concatenating to the whole text with every node id on exactly one line — and the driver's `snapshot` reads a screen over `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` in parts: on an over-budget fixture, in both layout modes, each part's lines equal their lines in the whole text, a password's line reads `MASKED_VALUE` in every part, and exactly one line reads `focused` after a click (`stand_snapshot_parts.rs`). The snapshot's diff (`Snapshot::diff`) is one more reader of that model: a text change is reported on the element whose accessible name it changes, by its id and never as a text-run entry, a hidden element leaves and returns with its descendants, and a focus move names exactly the controls whose `focused` reading moved (`stand_diff.rs`). Since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface an MCP tool result is one more reader of that model and of nothing else — a `snapshot` result is `to_text`'s output itself for a whole screen, equal byte for byte to `Session::run`'s screen text in both layout modes (`stand_mcp_tools.rs`), and, for a screen read in parts, its JSON line `{"text","part","parts"}` holding that part's text — through `serve_mcp` a walk's text blocks equal the JSON lines `Session::run` writes, in both layout modes (`stand_snapshot_parts.rs`), its crossing to an MCP client ratified by the founder (2026-10-10). Since 2026-10-12-self-description a password input typed through an MCP `type` reads `MASKED_VALUE` in the tool result, role `PasswordInput` and a non-empty name, the typed text in neither result, in both layout modes — a test-only element of the shared password page `fixtures::password_named` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs`), no stand task or app gaining one; and two further readers of the same model state closed words only: the node keys' help that `help` serves (each key's reading, the boolean model's two limits among them) and `DiffNode::differs`, a changed node naming the readings that differ from before the step in node-key order — the Flight Booker's Book names eight nodes — seven that only moved, each `differs` = `[bounds]`, and since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness `flight-book` itself, which the click now focuses, `differs` = `[focused, bounds]` (`stand_diff.rs`). Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot the driver's `screenshot` is one more reader of the model's bounds and of nothing else in it — an element shot, addressed by stable id and refused as every id-addressed call is, is the node's bounds rounded outward and cropped to the part that can be seen — and a shot changes nothing: no focus moves, `has_changes` stays false and the next diff is empty, in both layout modes (`stand_act_screenshot.rs`). Since 2026-11-07-ui-graph the read-only UI graph (`DioxusDocument::graph`, a `UiGraph`, behind `accessibility`) is one more reader beside the snapshot: one `GraphNode` per snapshot node in pre-order, carrying ids, component names, state names, handler event names, closed flag words and booleans only, never a value, with no second role or name mapping — `stand_graph` asserts in both layout modes that every graph node is a snapshot node and that a graph read changes nothing and holds no typed text. Since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here the driver's `actions` verb (`Session::actions`) is one more read-only reader: for every actionable node (`DioxusDocument::actionable_nodes`, each an `ActionableNode` of `id`, `owner` and `keyed`, read through the one crate-private actionable rule `Readings` it shares with `unkeyed_actionable` — focusable, one of 27 interactive roles, or current vdom-walk listeners holding an event other than `mounted`, so a listener a re-render removed is read by neither) it answers each id-taking verb with the cause `check_target` would refuse it with, changing nothing and writing ids, owner ids, verb and cause words and booleans only, never a value; `keyed` on the carriers is standing — the actionable-key check's wire form, true where the id holds no slash, and Cells' unpaged answer (678 nodes, 106,088 bytes) is a stated limit owned by residual `res-7cc5bi4k`.

- Actionable-key check (under `accessibility` only): `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable() -> Vec<UnkeyedActionable>` returns every actionable element whose id is a positional path, in document pre-order — actionable meaning focusable (`Node::is_focussable()`), or an interactive role on its accessibility node, or current listeners holding an event other than `mounted` (read from the vdom walk's `element_facts` through the crate-private `Readings`, never the `data-dioxus-id` mark, so an element whose listener a re-render removed is not counted), so a disabled control is held by its role and a hidden one by the other two. `UnkeyedActionable` carries `node` (a process-local `NodeId`), `id`, `tag`, `role: Option<Role>`, `focusable`, `interactive_role`, `listener` and `remedy()`; never text, a name or an attribute value. Read-only, logs nothing; beside it the read-only `DioxusDocument::actionable_nodes() -> Vec<ActionableNode>` (`ActionableNode { id, owner: Option<String>, keyed: bool }`, re-exported beside `UnkeyedActionable`) lists, over the UI graph's nodes in snapshot pre-order, each node the same actionable rule holds for or the graph gives an owner, `keyed` true where the id holds no `/`, both readers reading the one rule; its first wire form `ActionableNode`'s `keyed` reading (true where the id holds no `/`), which the driver's `actions` verb carries on every carrier, standing. The stand reads it empty on the four lean tasks and Home and, since 2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep, on Temperature Converter, Circle Drawer (its dialog open included) and Cells too (2 · 3 · 676 until then), and on the load page `stand::boot_load` mounts, its two elements keyed `load-fetch` · `load-done` — empty on all six served tasks (`stand_load_page`), keyed by author ids added as `id:` lines alone (`stand_actionable_keys`, `stand_non_lean_tasks`).

The driver's core (unpublished, no `[features]` of its own, no binary): a **session** — one headless app instance held by one process while commands arrive — the **command and refusal schema**, the one definition of what can be asked of the driver and of how it says no, the **executor** that runs a call on the held instance, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli the **command line** that carries a call out of the process, and since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the **MCP server** that serves the fourteen verbs as MCP tools over a caller's reader and writer (the `escher-session mcp` role), and since 2026-10-12-self-description the **self-description** (`describe`) that `help` answers on both surfaces, and since 2026-10-19-session-recording the **recording**: a session whose launcher names a recording directory keeps its answered calls at rest as one owner-only replayable check (`std` only, unix only like the socket), and since 2026-10-19-visual-lint the **visual lint** (`Session::lint` in process and the `lint` verb, the eighth instance verb, on every carrier (the socket's `call`, the command line, an MCP tool, `help`'s listing) and recorded — built by «Visual lint» (its gated part)), which reads the held screen and returns its layout and contrast defects as typed findings, which cross on the ratified carriers and rest in a kept check as the `lint` verb's answer — stable ids, the closed defect words and numbers, no page text, colour, control value or `NodeId` (a ratified boundary widening), and since 2026-11-07-ui-graph the **UI graph** (the `graph` verb, the ninth instance verb, on every carrier and recorded), which reads the held screen's graph through `DioxusDocument::graph` and answers stable ids, owner ids, component names, registered state names, handler event names, the declared writes, the closed flag words `undeclared` and `unconfirmed` and booleans, never a value, typed text or `NodeId` (a ratified boundary widening), and since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here the **actions read** (`Session::actions` and the `actions` verb, the tenth instance verb, on every carrier and recorded), which lists each actionable node of the held screen with what each id-taking verb would answer now, answering stable ids, owner ids, the table's verb words, the closed cause words and `keyed` booleans, never a value, typed text or `NodeId` (a ratified boundary widening). It is app-agnostic: the caller supplies the boot and the time step, and the crate names no app and no stand type. `Session::run` validates a call, looks its target up on the screen, refuses a target that cannot take the action, runs its verb, settles the instance and returns a typed `Outcome` — for a call made in process, and for one a host decoded from its socket. A call and its answer cross the socket (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10), and an MCP client's stdio (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»); since 2026-10-19-session-recording a recorded session's calls — the ids they named among them — rest in a kept check with its answers' digests and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, each answer kept whole — its line as the driver wrote it, masked as on every carrier, a shot's without its pixels — so the screens' ids, names, values, snapshot text, diffs, a lint's findings, a UI graph's names, closed flag words and booleans, and an actions answer's ids, owner ids, verb words, closed cause words and booleans rest there too, never logged (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-19, F1 A · F2 B · F3 B); a kept check replays through `Session::run` alone (`Check::replay`), and since 2026-11-08-handler-coverage the **coverage reader** (`handler_coverage` and the command line's `coverage` role) replays kept checks, each on a fresh session, and lists the UI graph's handlers no check exercised, and the repository's own two scripted stand checks are committed in git, the one exception to owner-only. A settle verb on the socket is a later route entry.

- The wire (`wire.rs`, crate-private, versioned `v3`, `v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording) is one request line and one reply line per connection: `hello v3` → `ok v3 pid= label= served= idle_expiry_s=`, `stop v3` → `ok v3 stopping`, `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` → `ok v3 accepted <json>` · `ok v3 refused <json>` · `ok v3 oversize` · `ok v3 recording-failed` (sent in place of the answer when the host's recording ended after the call, the client reading it as `RecordingFailed`), another version of a known word → `refused version`, anything else → `refused malformed`. Kinds are `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value are percent-escaped byte for byte and decoded strictly. A request is bounded at 16,384 bytes, a lifecycle reply at 128, an answer at 1,048,576 on its JSON line; each read and write at 2 s, a client's read of an answer at 30 s. **What the screen reads crosses it in an answer** — ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the mask), the snapshot's text and the diff — and an element id and typed text cross in (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10); no `NodeId` crosses. Inside the text and the diff an element that states one also reads selected, pressed or invalid — closed words in the text, booleans in a diff node, never an attribute's value as typed: an inventory fact of the ratified crossing, not a further widening (the founder, 2026-10-10), who set the rule with it — a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a widening; authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still is. The MCP surface was that next crossing question: since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the same content crosses to an MCP client in tool results over the `mcp` role's stdio, the request-id echo and the bounds above ratified by the founder with it (2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»); the next surface that carries any of it is a new crossing question — since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test the operator-driven live cold-agent run carries the stand's screen (element ids, accessible names and control values in snapshot texts and diffs, from this MCP server) on to the model provider, one run, on the founder's «Один запуск, до $3 (Рекомендую)» and «JSON-проверка с повтором (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-15). Since 2026-10-12-self-description the command line's stdout and the `mcp` role's stdio also carry the program's own fixed text, held as `'static` data of the one table — the `help` self-description, a session error's remedy and each tool's description with its result fields — riding those ratified carriers, and a changed node's `differs` crosses as a closed set by the rule of 2026-10-10 (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12); text from a page, a call or a screen, a new carrier or a new exit still widens. Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a shot's pixels cross in band on those carriers — its PNG as base64 inside the answer on the session socket and the command line's stdout, and as an MCP `image` block on the `mcp` role's stdio — screen content and no closed value set, with no new carrier, exit or path argument and the 1,048,576-byte bounds unchanged, a bigger image ending `oversize` / `AnswerTooLarge`: a boundary widening ratified by the founder (2026-10-12). Since 2026-10-19-visual-lint a lint's findings cross on those carriers and rest in a kept check as the `lint` verb's answer — stable ids, the closed defect words and numbers, no page text, colour, control value or `NodeId` — with no new carrier, exit, path argument, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening; since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts a screen over the snapshot budget crosses them in parts — `snapshot`'s optional `part` (a whole number, 1 to `MAX_PART` = 1000) in, one part's text with the closed counts `part` and `parts` out, a part past the last the empty text, a screen within the budget answering whole as before, over MCP a paged answer its JSON line — with no new verb, carrier, exit, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening. Since 2026-10-31-select-popup the select list crosses the ratified carriers only as a row's own `bounds` in the snapshot and the diff — `differs` naming `bounds`, a closed set inside the ratified crossing — and as pixels in a `screenshot`, with no new carrier, exit, cause, session error, node key, log field or span; an option's and a group's label leaving as pixels in every shot of an open list is a boundary widening, ratified. Since 2026-11-07-ui-graph the UI graph crosses the ratified carriers — the session socket's `call`, the command line and MCP, as a text block — and rests in a kept check as the `graph` verb's answer: stable ids, owner ids, component names, registered state names, handler event names, the declared writes the app authors, the closed flag words `undeclared` and `unconfirmed` and booleans, never a value, typed text or `NodeId`; each snapshot node carries the closed bool `clickable`; no new carrier, exit, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening. Since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here the actions answer crosses the ratified carriers — the session socket's `call`, the command line and MCP — and rests in a kept check as the `actions` verb's answer: `actions` takes no argument, one refused `malformed` with nothing run, and answers the whole screen at once, unpaged (Cells 106,088 bytes for 678 nodes, under the 1,048,576-byte bound), holding stable ids, owner ids, the table's verb words, the closed cause words and booleans, the `keyed` reading among them, never a value, typed text or `NodeId`; no new carrier, exit, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening. Since 2026-11-08-handler-coverage the command line's `coverage` role, `coverage <app> <check>...`, takes kept-check file paths its caller names as arguments: each path is read bounded and through `Check::from_bytes`, an unreadable, over-bound, non-check or other-app file refused `malformed` holding nothing of the path, and its answer is one line of ids, owner ids, event names and two counts on stdout, never a `NodeId`; no new socket message, MCP tool, verb, cause, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening.

- **Local IPC — the driver session socket (the founder's choice, 2026-10-07)** → `escher_driver::serve` binds `session.sock` in a caller-named state directory, created `0700` (a group- or other-open one refused), the socket `0600`: reachable by the owning user only, with no other authentication; the wire is a closed line grammar at `v3` (`v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording) — `hello`, `stop` and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…`, percent-escaped and decoded strictly — with a 16,384-byte request bound, a 2 s I/O bound (30 s on a client's read of an answer), refusals running nothing; a lifecycle reply (at most 128 bytes) carries a pid, a label of `a-z0-9-`, a count and the idle expiry, and a call's answer (at most 1,048,576 bytes, `oversize` past it; since 2026-10-19-session-recording a call after which the host's recording ended is answered the fixed `ok v3 recording-failed` in place of its answer, the call having run, read by the client as `SessionError::RecordingFailed`) carries what the screen reads — ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the fixed mask), the snapshot's text, the diff, a lint's findings (stable ids, closed defect words and numbers) and the UI graph (an accepted `graph`'s line `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…]}`: ids, owner ids, component names, registered state names, handler event names, the closed flag words `undeclared` · `unconfirmed` and booleans, never a control value, typed text or `NodeId`; a boundary widening, ratified) and the actions answer (an accepted `actions`'s line `{"nodes":[{"id":…,"owner":…,"keyed":…,"verbs":[{"verb":…,"cause":…}]}]}`: ids, owner ids, `keyed` booleans, the table's verb words and closed cause words, never a control value, typed text or `NodeId`; a boundary widening, ratified), the text and the diff since 2026-10-10-snapshot-states also holding three state readings (selected, pressed, invalid) as closed words and booleans and since 2026-11-07-ui-graph a `clickable` reading (a closed bool: the bare word in the text only when true, a diff key always, `differs` able to name it) and since 2026-10-12-self-description a changed node's `differs`, a list of closed words, never an attribute's value as typed, an open select list's row reading its own `bounds` in the text and the diff, `differs` naming `bounds`, `NodeState` holding no field of the list, `NODE_FIELDS` fourteen (`clickable`, a closed bool, after `focused`) and no `expanded` node key standing — inside the ratified crossing, not a further widening (the founder, 2026-10-10, who set the rule with it: a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a widening; authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still is); since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot an answer also takes the screen's pixels out — an accepted `screenshot`'s PNG as base64 inside its JSON line, the whole screen or one element's visible part, a password input in it painted masked, a shot of an open select list also taking a page's option labels and group `label`s out as pixels, the shot's fields unmoved (a boundary widening, ratified), under the unchanged 1,048,576-byte bound (the in-band image the founder chose, 2026-10-12); a call brings an element id and typed text in; no `NodeId` crosses — a second widening, ratified by the founder (2026-10-10); a host with no request answered for its idle expiry (1,800 s) ends as on `stop`; unix only.

- **Local stdio — the driver's MCP server (since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface; the crossing ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»)** → `escher_driver::serve_mcp`, run by `escher-session mcp` as a child an MCP client spawns under the invoking user: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on its stdin and stdout, no listener, port, socket or authentication — the trust boundary is the process holding its stdio;
